data.narrative:
Matter is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $21M to date. The relevant comp universe spans 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, though no sufficiently tight peer cohort exists at identical stage and valuation tier to support direct median benchmarking.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier, standard for Seed-to-next-stage advancement, to a $14M base value (derived from total raised as proxy). This method yields an implied valuation of $35M. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable due to insufficient granular comparables: while 11 same-sector peers exist in robotics and manufacturing, only 1 same-stage and 1 adjacent-stage peer met filter criteria, falling short of the 3-datapoint minimum required for statistically meaningful median derivation. Using the broader all-sector peer set would introduce material distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30M to $40M, centered on a $35M median. This range reflects conservative application of stage-based progression logic against a capital-raised baseline. Key uncertainties include the lack of tight peer benchmarking data at Seed stage within robotics specifically, and the absence of disclosed revenue or unit economics that would enable revenue multiple or cash-flow-based approaches. The range should be updated as comparable transactions emerge or if Matter discloses material operational metrics.
